newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US T-bonds seen poised for further gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US T-bonds seen poised for further gains.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures are poised for further gains in the intermediate term after Friday's strong rally, although they might need some consolidation before going sharply higher, analysts said.
"We decisively blasted above that trendline from the December highs on Friday," said Terence Gabriel, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc.

With momentum indicators for various time-frames building up, Gabriel said T-bonds could rise a point or so in the very near term before bumping into significant resistance, where they would probably correct before another big move up.

He saw tough resistance for September T-bond futures at the 111-27/32 to 111-28/32 area, where the 61.8-percent retracement of the December-April decline and a descending weekly one-by-one Gann line from the January 1996 high adjusted for the September contract came in.
"I would expect that on the first test of these levels you would get retrenchment," Gabriel said, adding that the contract should then resume its uptrend toward its February high at 113-9/32.
The Septembers were off 10/32 at 110-29/32 in late morning business.
Given the positive momentum, pullbacks from here should be limited, perhaps toward 110-1/2, Gabriel said.

He noted that the weekly moving average convergence/divergence had turned positive on Friday's rally, and the daily ADX indicator, which shows the strength of a directional movement, was rising rapidly.

"I think they suggest that there's good trend momentum behind this breakout," he said, adding that strength in banking stocks and the recent slide in crude oil prices also reflected a favorable environment.
John Gambino of JBG Technical Analysis said the market was in the third leg of a five-wave sequence to the upside that started from the April 11 low.

"This one (the current leg), which started on May 28, has quite a bit of momentum and is indicative of a third wave," he said. "That being the case, it stretches the target up to 115 to 116, which coincides with the December high."
While pullbacks like today's were inevitable, they were just "white noise," Gambino said.
He projected support at about 110-22/32 but said the market was unlikely to pull back that deep.
